messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure in the test `testSkipNotEncodedCRLF` arises from the decoding behavior of `QuotedPrintableCodec.decode`. The test inputs a string containing CR (carriage return) and LF (line feed) characters that are not part of encoded hex sequences, specifically including sequences like `=20=\r\n\r` which are intended as soft line breaks in quoted-printable encoding.

The `decode` method calls `decodeQuotedPrintable` on the byte array form of the input. In `decodeQuotedPrintable`, each byte is inspected. When an escape character `=` (ESCAPE_CHAR) is found, it expects the next two characters to be hexadecimal digits. These are combined to form the decoded byte. If the next character sequence is a CR followed by LF (a soft line break), the code treats it successfully as an encoded space but does not explicitly skip the soft line breaks if they are not properly formatted.

Importantly, the handling of soft line breaks seems incomplete or incorrect. The method does not explicitly ignore the soft line breaks `=\r\n` as required by the quoted-printable standard, and it simply reads the next two hexadecimal digits after `=` without checking if the next character is a CR (`\r`) indicating a soft line break. This causes decoding to fail or include extra unwanted characters.

This behavior matches the current bug report stating that Wiki example for quoted-printable (which uses soft line breaks like `=20=\r\n`) does not decode but throws an exception.

The failing test’s input string contains CR and LF characters that should be skipped because they are part of the soft line break mechanism in quoted-printable encoding, but the decoder does not skip these correctly. Instead, it tries to decode `=20=\r\n\r` literally and fails or generates incorrect output.

Thus, the bug is in the handling of soft line breaks (i.e. `=\r\n`) in `decodeQuotedPrintable`: It fails to detect and skip these soft line breaks properly, causing incorrect decoding results or exceptions when such sequences appear.

Recent bug reports are unrelated and do not add relevant information on this issue.

Summary: The bug is caused by `decodeQuotedPrintable` improperly processing soft line breaks, which leads to failed decoding or errors, failing to conform to the quoted-printable specification and leading to the failed test and reported Wikipedia example failure.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
